Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g1²·g2⁻¹, g1·g2·g1⁻¹⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1²·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det ≈ 3.5980409 (a root of x³ − 27/4x² + 117/8x − 3025/256) is real (numerically: |Im| < 10⁻¹⁰) and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.20535186π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 6; no such m has (g1²·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1²·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹·g2² fixes the fixed point of the parabolic g1·g2·g1⁻¹ and multiplies its translation by μ ≈ 1.259921 + 2.1822473i, |μ| ≈ 2.5198421 ≠ 1. The common fixed point and μ are exact (g·N·g⁻¹ = μ·N over K, for the nilpotent part N of the parabolic), and so are μ⁴ ≠ 1 and μ⁶ ≠ 1. The parabolics (g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹·g2²)ⁿ·(g1·g2·g1⁻¹)·(g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹·g2²)⁻ⁿ translate by μⁿτ, which shrinks to 0 as n → −∞: non-trivial elements converging to the identity, so the group is not discrete.
